Standard populations

Source: R/derive-quantities.R
standard_population.Rd

  • "esp2013": the revised European Standard Population 2013 (Eurostat 2013, Revision of the European Standard Population, report KS-RA-13-028), in 5-year groups with 0, 1-4 and 95+, total 100,000;

  • "esp1976": the European Standard Population of 1976 (0, 1-4, 5-year groups, 85+), total 100,000;

  • "who2000": the WHO World Standard Population, world average 2000-2025 (Ahmad et al. 2001), 5-year groups to 100+; the published weights sum to 100,035 and are used as published (rates are divided by the sum of the weights).

Usage

standard_population(name = c("esp2013", "esp1976", "who2000"))

Arguments

name

Name of the standard.

Value

A data.table with age_lo, age_hi, weight; the name is in attribute "name".

Details

A national standard is used by passing a data frame with age_lo, age_hi (Inf for the open group) and weight to the standard argument of asr().

References

Ahmad OB, Boschi-Pinto C, Lopez AD, Murray CJL, Lozano R, Inoue M (2001). Age standardization of rates: a new WHO standard. GPE Discussion Paper Series No. 31. World Health Organization, Geneva.

Examples

standard_population()
#>     age_lo age_hi weight
#>      <num>  <num>  <num>
#>  1:      0      1   1000
#>  2:      1      5   4000
#>  3:      5     10   5500
#>  4:     10     15   5500
#>  5:     15     20   5500
#>  6:     20     25   6000
#>  7:     25     30   6000
#>  8:     30     35   6500
#>  9:     35     40   7000
#> 10:     40     45   7000
#> 11:     45     50   7000
#> 12:     50     55   7000
#> 13:     55     60   6500
#> 14:     60     65   6000
#> 15:     65     70   5500

#> 17:     75     80   4000
